data.name: Farhand
data.gender_notes: Farhand is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic words 'Far' meaning 'distant' and 'Hand' meaning 'helper'. The name Farhand signifies someone who is a helper or supporter from a distance. The name Farhand carries the meaning “Exalted, Noble” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Farhand usually hope their child will grow to embody exalted, noble and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes divine guidance and protection, representing the idea that even when we feel alone, God is always with us, supporting us in our journey through life.
data.etymology: Farhand belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Exalted, Noble.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Farhand total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Qutaybah, Al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Qur'an (The Comprehensive Explanation of the Rules of the Qur'an).
historical_references.context: Ibn Qutaybah describes Farhad as a Persian vizier who was ordered by the queen to construct a bridge across the Araxes River. When the queen learned that Farhad had fallen in love with her daughter Shirin, she ordered her daughter to be killed. Devastated by this news, Farhad committed suicide by jumping into the river.

historical_references.reference: Al-Tabari, The History of al-Tabari: The Foundation of the Community. Translated by M.V. de Houtmeyers.
historical_references.context: Al-Tabari tells the story of Farhad, the Persian vizier who was ordered by the queen to construct a bridge across the Araxes River. During the construction, the queen learned that her daughter Shirin had been secretly seeing Farhad. In her anger, she ordered her daughter to be killed. When Farhad learned of this, he was devastated and committed suicide by jumping into the river.
